author: @donnajenkins4721
text: The dairy industry maintains a significant presence in Washington, D.C., spending millions annually to influence agricultural policy, nutritional guidelines, and environmental regulations. Financial Investment Annual Spending: The dairy industry spent approximately $6.9 million on federal lobbying in 2020. In the 2024 cycle, total spending remains substantial, with major players continuing to invest heavily in legislative influence. Top Spenders (2024): Land O’Lakes: ~$2.49 million National Milk Producers Federation (NMPF): ~$1.80 million International Dairy Foods Association (IDFA): ~$1.01 million Dairy Farmers of America (DFA): ~$760,000 Political Leanings: Contributions historically favor Republicans, with roughly 71–75% of industry donations typically going to GOP candidates. Key Policy Priorities School Nutrition: A major recent success for the lobby was the 2026 bill allowing whole milk back into school lunches, overturning previous restrictions on saturated fat. The industry has long fought to keep milk as a mandatory or primary offering in federal school meal programs. Farm Bill & Subsidies: Lobbyists advocate for the multi-billion dollar Farm Bill, which secures corporate farm subsidies and insurance programs. Some reports indicate that up to 20% of dairy revenue comes from direct or indirect government subsidies. Climate Change: Industry groups have been accused of using "fossil fuel tactics" to block or weaken climate legislation that would limit methane emissions or production. They have also lobbied for "climate-smart" feed additives to address environmental concerns without reducing herd sizes. Trade and Labor: Lobbying efforts focus on enforcing international trade deals and expanding agricultural visa programs to address labor shortages on dairy farms. Marketing and "Checkoff" Programs The USDA-overseen "Checkoff" program collects mandatory fees from producers to fund massive pro-dairy marketing campaigns. Recent subtle campaigns include sponsoring "wellness weekends" for media editors and branded content with digital outlets to promote "milk-forward" recipes. An independent evaluation found that for every dollar spent on cheese promotion, farmers earned back $3.27.
